subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default policy should OpenClaw apply when plugins or external integrations register recurring model-backed cron jobs: default-disabled consent, explicit per-job model requirements, budget/circuit breakers, and provenance/doctor UI as one coordinated change or split follow-ups?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but changing cron activation and cost-safety defaults can affect existing users, plugin schedules, provider routing, and upgrades, so automation should not choose the product and security policy alone.

options.title: Define one coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Treat externally registered recurring model-backed cron jobs as a security/cost-sensitive surface and design activation consent, model-cost guardrails, provenance, doctor/update previews, and circuit breakers together.

options.title: Split by existing canonical issues
options.body: Move reason-aware retry, gateway spend budgets, and schedule provenance to their existing open issues while keeping this issue for default-disabled external job activation only.

options.title: Preserve current defaults
options.body: Keep external cron jobs enabled by default and rely on existing per-job model overrides, generic backoff, and operator review for now.

recommendation.title: Define one coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Treat externally registered recurring model-backed cron jobs as a security/cost-sensitive surface and design activation consent, model-cost guardrails, provenance, doctor/update previews, and circuit breakers together.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent cron scheduler history and is a strong routing owner for the product/security policy choice that spans cron runtime and compatibility.
